title: Arya Vysya / Komati
about: Arya Vysya is a well-known Telugu-speaking community with a long association with commerce, entrepreneurship, education and community institutions. Members are found across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and many other parts of India and abroad.
intro: The community has historically maintained strong social networks through associations, temples, charitable organisations and business groups. Today, its members are active across business, technology, medicine, education and professional services.
history: The community has deep historical roots in South India, particularly in the Telugu regions. Traditionally associated with trade and commerce, Arya Vysya groups gradually expanded into modern industry, professional careers and global entrepreneurship.

title: Brahmin
about: Brahmin communities are present across India and include numerous regional and linguistic traditions. In the Telugu states, several Brahmin groups have contributed to education, literature, religious scholarship, administration and professional fields.
intro: The community is diverse, with different traditions, family lineages and regional practices. Members today work across virtually every profession and sector.
history: Historically, Brahmin communities were associated with scholarship, teaching, religious learning and preservation of classical knowledge. Over time, members entered administration, science, technology, business, medicine and many other modern professions.

title: Reddy
about: Reddy is a prominent Telugu-speaking community found primarily in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, with a significant presence elsewhere in India and overseas.
intro: Members of the community are active in agriculture, business, public service, education, medicine, technology and numerous professional sectors.
history: Historically connected with agriculture, land administration and regional leadership in the Telugu-speaking areas, the community expanded over generations into urban professions, entrepreneurship and global careers.

title: Kamma
about: Kamma is a major Telugu-speaking community with a substantial presence in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and among Telugu communities abroad.
intro: The community today has a strong presence in agriculture, business, education, technology, cinema, healthcare and entrepreneurship.
history: Historically associated with agriculture and regional landholding in parts of coastal Andhra and neighbouring regions, members later moved extensively into commerce, industry, education and professional sectors.

title: Kapu
about: Kapu is a large Telugu-speaking community with several regional groups across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members are engaged in agriculture, business, employment, public service and a wide range of professional occupations.
history: Kapu communities have historically been associated with cultivation and rural society in different parts of the Telugu region. With urbanisation and education, the community has diversified significantly into modern professions and entrepreneurship.

title: Balija
about: Balija communities are found across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and other parts of South India.
intro: The community has historically participated in trade, agriculture and local commerce and today includes members from a wide range of occupations.
history: Historical references connect different Balija groups with trade and commercial activity across South India. Over time, regional branches developed distinct customs and occupational patterns.

title: Telaga
about: Telaga is a Telugu-speaking community found mainly in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members are present in agriculture, government employment, business and modern professional sectors.
history: The community has longstanding roots in the Telugu region, with historical associations varying by district and locality. Over generations, members have moved from predominantly rural occupations into diverse urban and professional careers.

title: Ontari
about: Ontari is a Telugu community found in parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members today participate in agriculture, employment, business and various professional fields.
history: The community has regional historical roots in the Telugu-speaking areas. Its traditions and historical accounts can differ by locality, reflecting the diversity of family and regional histories within the community.

title: Munnuru Kapu
about: Munnuru Kapu is a significant community particularly associated with Telangana.
intro: Members are involved in agriculture, business, public service, education and a growing range of professional sectors.
history: The community has long-standing roots in the Telangana region and historically had strong connections with agriculture and village economies. Modern education and urbanisation have led to increasing diversification.

title: Turpu Kapu
about: Turpu Kapu is a Telugu-speaking community with a strong presence in the northern coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring areas.
intro: The community is active in agriculture, employment, business and professional occupations.
history: Historically rooted in the eastern regions of the Telugu-speaking area, Turpu Kapu families have been part of agricultural and local economic life for generations and have increasingly moved into urban professions.

title: Velama
about: Velama is a Telugu-speaking community with a historical presence in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
intro: Members are active in agriculture, business, public life, education and modern professions.
history: Historical accounts associate different Velama groups with agriculture, regional administration and local leadership. The community has developed distinct regional traditions over several centuries.

title: Raju / Kshatriya
about: Raju communities are found primarily in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and have several regional family traditions.
intro: Members today are active in business, agriculture, government, education, technology and professional services.
history: Various Raju families preserve traditions connecting them with historical ruling, military and landholding lineages. Specific genealogical accounts vary considerably between regions and families.

title: Padmashali
about: Padmashali is a Telugu-speaking community historically associated with weaving and textile craftsmanship.
intro: Today, members work across textiles, business, government, technology, education and many other professional sectors.
history: The community has a long connection with handloom weaving and textile production in the Telugu states. Industrialisation, education and migration led many families into new professions while weaving traditions continue in several regions.

title: Devanga
about: Devanga is a South Indian community traditionally associated with weaving and textile production.
intro: Members are found across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and other regions and today participate in diverse occupations.
history: Historically connected with textile craftsmanship and weaving networks, Devanga communities developed across different linguistic regions of South India and gradually diversified into commerce and professional careers.

title: Pattusali
about: Pattusali is a community historically associated with silk and textile weaving in parts of South India.
intro: Members today work in textile businesses as well as education, employment, industry and modern professional sectors.
history: The community's historical identity is closely connected with skilled weaving and textile craftsmanship. Changing economic conditions encouraged many families to diversify beyond traditional occupations.

title: Goud
about: Goud is a significant Telugu-speaking community, particularly in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
intro: Members today are active in agriculture, business, government employment, education and professional sectors.
history: Goud communities have long-standing roots in village and agricultural economies of the Telugu region. Traditional occupations varied regionally, and the community has substantially diversified in modern times.

title: Ediga
about: Ediga communities are found across parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and neighbouring South Indian regions.
intro: Members are engaged in agriculture, business, employment and a wide variety of modern professions.
history: The community has a long regional history in South India, with occupational traditions differing between areas. Education, migration and economic change have contributed to broad professional diversification.

title: Yadava / Golla
about: Yadava and Golla communities have a widespread presence across the Telugu states and other parts of India.
intro: Traditionally associated with livestock and pastoral activities in many areas, members today work across agriculture, business, government and professional sectors.
history: Pastoral and cattle-rearing traditions have been an important part of the history of many Yadava and Golla groups. Over time, settlements, agriculture, education and urbanisation brought substantial occupational change.

title: Kuruma
about: Kuruma is a community found particularly in Telangana and neighbouring regions.
intro: The community has historical connections with pastoral life and sheep rearing, while members today participate in many occupations and professions.
history: Kuruma groups have long been associated with pastoral and rural economies. Social and economic changes have gradually expanded educational, business and professional opportunities.

title: Mudiraj
about: Mudiraj is a large community with a significant presence in Telangana and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
intro: Members today are engaged in agriculture, business, government employment, education and numerous professional fields.
history: The community has a long regional history in the Deccan and Telugu-speaking areas. Historical occupations and traditions varied considerably by district and family group.

title: Boya / Valmiki
about: Boya and Valmiki communities are present across several parts of South India, including Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members today participate in agriculture, employment, business, education and professional sectors.
history: The communities have diverse regional histories and traditions. Different groups have historically been associated with rural livelihoods, local service roles and other occupations, with considerable change over time.

title: Bestha / Gangaputra
about: Bestha and Gangaputra communities are found in the Telugu states and have historical connections with water-based livelihoods in many regions.
intro: Members today are involved in fisheries, agriculture, business, employment and various professional occupations.
history: Fishing, boating and other water-related activities were historically important to many families. Economic diversification and education have led to an increasingly broad range of careers.

title: Agnikula Kshatriya
about: Agnikula Kshatriya communities are found in coastal and other parts of Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring regions.
intro: Members participate in fishing-related occupations, business, education, employment and professional fields.
history: Different regional groups have distinct historical traditions and community narratives. Coastal livelihoods and maritime occupations have played an important role in the history of many families.

title: Settibalija
about: Settibalija is a Telugu-speaking community found particularly in Andhra Pradesh.
intro: Members today are active in agriculture, business, employment, education and professional sectors.
history: The community has long-standing roots in the Telugu-speaking region, with traditional occupations differing by locality. Modernisation and education have brought extensive occupational diversification.

title: Gavara
about: Gavara is a community with a notable presence in northern coastal Andhra Pradesh and nearby regions.
intro: Members participate in agriculture, trade, business, employment and modern professional careers.
history: Historically rooted in the coastal Andhra region, Gavara families have been connected with local agriculture and commerce, while later generations increasingly entered urban and professional sectors.

title: Perika
about: Perika is a Telugu-speaking community found across parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members are engaged in agriculture, commerce, employment and a range of professional occupations.
history: The community has regional historical traditions connected with trade and rural economic activity. Specific historical accounts can vary between different areas and family groups.

title: Uppara
about: Uppara communities are present in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and other parts of South India.
intro: Members today work in construction-related activities, agriculture, business, government and diverse professions.
history: Historically, some Uppara groups were associated with earthwork, construction and related occupations. Over time, the community expanded into many other fields through education and economic mobility.

title: Vaddera
about: Vaddera is a South Indian community with a presence in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and neighbouring states.
intro: Members today participate in construction, infrastructure, business, employment and professional sectors.
history: Different Vaddera groups have historically been associated with stonework, earthwork and construction-related skills. Modern generations have increasingly diversified into education, business and salaried professions.

title: Kummari
about: Kummari is a Telugu-speaking community historically associated with pottery and ceramic craftsmanship.
intro: Members today work in traditional crafts as well as business, education, government and many other professions.
history: Pottery has been an important traditional occupation for generations, supplying household and agricultural needs. Industrial production and urbanisation encouraged many families to pursue additional occupations.

title: Rajaka
about: Rajaka is a community found widely across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members today participate in service businesses, agriculture, employment, education and a broad range of professional careers.
history: The community historically performed specialised service occupations in villages and towns. Economic modernisation and education have significantly broadened occupational opportunities.

title: Nai Brahmin / Mangali
about: Nai Brahmin and Mangali communities are found across the Telugu states and have longstanding regional traditions.
intro: Members today are active in personal services, business, government, education and numerous modern professions.
history: Traditional service occupations formed an important part of the community's earlier economic role. Over generations, occupational and educational diversification has expanded considerably.

title: Viswakarma
about: Viswakarma is a broad artisan community found across South India and other parts of the country.
intro: The community includes families historically associated with skilled crafts such as metalwork, carpentry, jewellery and related artisan professions. Members today work across industry, engineering, business and professional fields.
history: Viswakarma traditions have long been connected with skilled craftsmanship and technical knowledge. Different regional occupational groups gradually developed specialised identities while retaining broader community connections.

title: Kamsali
about: Kamsali is a Telugu artisan community historically associated particularly with metal and jewellery craftsmanship.
intro: Members today work in jewellery, business, engineering, technology, education and numerous other sectors.
history: Skilled metalworking and goldsmithing traditions have been central to the history of many Kamsali families. Modern industrial and professional opportunities have expanded the community's occupational base.

title: Kammari
about: Kammari is a Telugu artisan community historically associated with ironwork, tools and metal craftsmanship.
intro: Members today participate in industry, engineering, business, skilled trades and professional sectors.
history: Traditional blacksmithing and metalworking played an important role in agricultural and village economies. Technological change gradually transformed traditional occupations and created new career pathways.

title: Vadrangi
about: Vadrangi is a Telugu artisan community traditionally associated with carpentry and wood craftsmanship.
intro: Members today work in carpentry, construction, interior design, engineering, business and many other professional areas.
history: Woodworking skills were historically essential for homes, agricultural equipment and community infrastructure. Over time, members expanded into modern construction, furniture, design and professional careers.

title: Kanchari
about: Kanchari is an artisan community historically associated with metal craft and related skilled occupations.
intro: Members today participate in traditional crafts as well as industry, trade, education and professional employment.
history: Metal craftsmanship has been an important part of the community's occupational heritage. Modern manufacturing and education have led to wider professional diversification.

title: Medara
about: Medara is a South Indian community traditionally associated with bamboo, cane and related craft work in many areas.
intro: Members today participate in handicrafts, agriculture, business, employment and professional sectors.
history: Bamboo and cane craftsmanship historically provided essential household and agricultural products. Industrialisation and changing markets encouraged diversification into other occupations.

title: Jangam
about: Jangam communities are found across parts of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and other regions of South India.
intro: The community has diverse religious, cultural and occupational traditions and today includes members from a wide range of professions.
history: Jangam traditions have historical connections with Shaiva religious traditions in parts of the Deccan and South India. Community practices and histories vary considerably by region.

title: Banjara / Lambadi
about: Banjara and Lambadi communities are widely distributed across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and many other Indian states.
intro: The community has a distinct cultural identity, language traditions and regional social institutions. Members today participate in agriculture, business, government, education and professional careers.
history: Banjaras historically had important roles in mobile trade and transport across large parts of India. Over time, many communities became settled while retaining distinctive cultural and social traditions.

title: Yerukala
about: Yerukala is a community found particularly in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: The community has distinct regional traditions and today participates in education, employment, agriculture, business and professional sectors.
history: Yerukala groups have long-standing histories in the Telugu region, with traditional livelihoods varying across areas. Settlement, education and changing economic conditions have led to substantial social and occupational transformation.

title: Mala
about: Mala is a large Telugu-speaking community with a significant presence in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members are active across education, public service, business, technology, medicine, politics, arts and numerous other professions.
history: Mala communities have deep historical roots in the Telugu region. Their social and economic history reflects major changes brought by education, urbanisation, public employment and social reform movements.

title: Madiga
about: Madiga is a major community with a substantial presence in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring states.
intro: Members today participate in education, public service, business, politics, technology, arts and a broad range of professional fields.
history: Madiga communities have long-standing roots in the Deccan and Telugu-speaking regions. Their modern history has been shaped significantly by education, urbanisation, social movements and expanding professional opportunities.

title: Chakali
about: Chakali is a Telugu community with a longstanding presence in villages and towns across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
intro: Members today are engaged in service businesses, agriculture, employment, education, entrepreneurship and a wide variety of modern professions.
history: The community historically performed specialised service occupations within local economies. Over generations, education, technology, migration and urbanisation have led to considerable occupational diversification.
